root_cause.text: In ntfs3’s `ntfs_get_frame_pages()` path, newly allocated folios were created without zero-initialization, so when `ni_read_frame()` was skipped and the compressed frame was only partially written, stale uninitialized bytes in the folio could later be read by `longest_match_std()` during `ntfs_compress_write()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says “new folios are allocated without being marked uptodate and ni_read_frame() is skipped… some reserved folios may remain only partially filled, leaving the rest memory uninitialized,” and the patch fixes this by changing `__filemap_get_folio(..., gfp_mask)` to `__filemap_get_folio(..., gfp_mask | __GFP_ZERO)`, explicitly zeroing newly allocated folios in `fs/ntfs3/file.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure NTFS allocates zeroed folios when fetching frame pages to avoid exposing or using stale page contents.
intent_record.what: In ntfs_get_frame_pages(), the gfp_mask argument passed to __filemap_get_folio() was changed from gfp_mask to gfp_mask | __GFP_ZERO.
intent_record.how: This causes newly allocated folios returned by __filemap_get_folio() to be zero-initialized instead of containing uninitialized memory, which affects the contents of pages created on demand during this path.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure NTFS allocates zeroed folios when fetching frame pages to avoid exposing or using stale page contents.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it ensures newly allocated folios are zero-initialized in the ntfs_get_frame_pages() path, preventing stale uninitialized bytes from being read later during compression.

candidates.rationale: This is the allocation path for frame pages. In the vulnerable code, it requested a new folio without zero-initialization, allowing stale bytes to remain in freshly allocated memory and later be consumed by compression logic when the frame was only partially written.

These flags show the folio is created if absent, but there is no zeroing-related flag in the pre-fix path. That omission is directly responsible for newly allocated folios containing uninitialized data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the folio allocation path in ntfs_get_frame_pages(). In the pre-fix code, the folio could be newly created without zero-initialization, leaving stale bytes in memory that later could be read during compression when the frame was only partially written.

These flags request creation of the folio if absent, but do not include any zeroing behavior. That omission allowed freshly allocated folios to contain uninitialized data, which is the root cause of stale bytes being consumed later by longest_match_std().

That behavior is not present in this snippet: there is no zero-initialization issue visible here, no read of uninitialized data, and no compression logic. Also, the fix is not shown here either; the code neither adds zeroing nor otherwise prevents the stale-byte read. So the vulnerable construct is absent from this function body, and this snippet alone does not show the later bug.
